turns.en: If you've got cross-jurisdictional stuff, then why on earth are you looking at cross-jurisdictional stuff? Who is that benefiting? If you have multiple layers of fees, who's getting paid, why are they getting paid?
turns.zh: 如果你有跨司法辖区的东西，那你到底为什么要碰跨司法辖区的东西？那在让谁受益？如果你有多层费用，谁在拿钱、他们为什么拿钱？

turns.en: Why do you need multiple levels of fees? Why does it need to be this complicated? If you have cross-currency, why on earth if you've got cross-currency stuff in there, there's another red flag and another complexity risk.
turns.zh: 你为什么需要多重费用层级？它为什么需要这么复杂？如果你里面有跨币种的东西——那简直是另一个危险信号、另一种复杂性风险。

turns.en: You should be looking at this, asking questions and being the most annoying person that you possibly can because your role is not to sell products.
turns.zh: 你应该去审视它、问问题，并且尽你所能做那个最让人厌烦的人，因为你的角色不是卖产品。

turns.en: Your role isn't to impress the person that comes to you with that product. Your absolute responsibility is to act in the best interests of your client.
turns.zh: 你的角色不是去讨好那个拿着这个产品来找你的人。你绝对的职责是为客户的最佳利益行事。

turns.en: And if you wouldn't sell it to your family, why on earth are you considering selling it to any of your clients? Oh, sing it, sister. I just saw too much of this.
turns.zh: 如果你都不会把它卖给家人，你凭什么考虑把它卖给你的任何客户？哦，说得太对了，姐妹。我见得实在太多了。

turns.en: Most of all of my career was based around stuff that the advisors didn't really understand. And then they didn't understand the downside. And they couldn't talk about the downside and they couldn't anticipate the downside.
turns.zh: 我职业生涯里绝大多数的东西，都建立在顾问其实并不真正理解的基础上。然后他们不理解下行的风险，他们谈不了下行风险，他们也预见不了下行风险。

turns.en: And when the downside happened, they said, oh, well, nobody foresaw that. It wasn't our fault. It was your fault because you were too greedy, client.
turns.zh: 而当下行真的发生时，他们说：哦，没人预见得到，那不是我们的错——那是你的错，因为你太贪了，客户。

turns.en: And so I was doing my best. I gave you this great product and it's just not my problem or my fault. We are on the same page on investments should be very boring.
turns.zh: 于是我一直在尽力，我给了你一个很棒的产品，这不是我的问题、也不是我的错。我们在"投资应该非常无聊"这一点上是一致的。

turns.en: You said you don't think your clients need the more complex stuff. I don't think most people need the more complex stuff that gets sold to more people than it should be sold to.
turns.zh: 你说你觉得你的客户不需要那些更复杂的东西。我觉得大多数人不需要那些更复杂的东西——而它被卖给了太多本不该被卖给的人。

turns.en: I'm curious, Philippa, in all of the cases that you've seen, you talked about how there wasn't an obvious way to identify the people doing misconduct before the fact.
turns.zh: 我很好奇，Philippa，在你见过的所有案子里，你谈到过在事情发生之前，并没有一种显而易见的方法来识别那些正在做不当行为的人。

turns.en: Do you think there's a relationship, though, between the financial literacy of the victims and the propensity to be victimized? It's a really interesting question.
turns.zh: 不过你觉得，受害者的金融素养水平与被侵害的倾向之间，存在某种关系吗？这是个很有意思的问题。

turns.en: So I acted for anyone from calm mechanics to teachers, to hedge fund managers, to doctors, to the whole gamut of financially sophisticated to financially unsophisticated.
turns.zh: 我为各种各样的人代理过，从汽车修理工，到老师，到对冲基金经理，到医生，从金融上很成熟到很不成熟的整个光谱。

turns.en: I acted for over a thousand British steel workers who were very much not financially sophisticated. And I don't mean that in any rude way. They simply weren't.
turns.zh: 我代理过一千多名英国钢铁工人，他们非常不是那种金融上成熟的人。我说这话毫无冒犯之意，他们就是不懂。

turns.en: But frankly, who is sophisticated to the extent that you might need to be to second guess a complex product? Who really is not in the financial services industry and advising on it understands how pensions work.
turns.zh: 但坦率讲，谁能真正达到那种"你为了质疑一个复杂产品所需要具备的成熟度"？谁——真的——不在金融服务业、不在给它出建议的范围内——懂得养老金是怎么运作的？

turns.en: I actually don't think that there is a direct correlation between financial sophistication and getting caught up in this stuff. It is far more emotional than anything else.
turns.zh: 我实际上不认为金融成熟度和被卷入这类事情之间存在直接的关联。它更多是情绪使然，而非其他任何东西。

turns.en: So when I talk about the steel workers who were transferred out of their final salary pension scheme, that was all emotional. But you don't want Tata to have your money.
turns.zh: 所以当我谈那些被从确定给付型养老金计划（final salary pension scheme）里转出来的钢铁工人，那全是情绪化的。可你不会想把你的钱留给 Tata 吧。

turns.en: You want that to go to your family, don't you, when you die? So it was all emotional decisions and this kind of white coat relationship. You know better than me.
turns.zh: "你死的时候，你想让那笔钱给你的家人，不是吗？"所以那全是一个个情绪化的决定，加上这种白大褂式的关系：你比我懂。

turns.en: The regulator has authorized you. Therefore, you have a tick in that box. Therefore, I should trust you. You know what to do. And actually, it's kind of too difficult.
turns.zh: 监管方授权了你。因此你在那一项上打了个勾。因此我应该信任你。你知道该怎么做。而其实，这太难了。

turns.en: I'm too busy doing my stuff. I want to delegate this. I want somebody else to take responsibility for it. Let's go for it. And as I said earlier, I cannot tell you how many of my clients said to me.
turns.zh: 我太忙我自己的事了，我想把这件事委托出去，我想让别人来为它负责。咱们上吧。正如我之前所说，我没法告诉你我有多少客户对我说过：

turns.en: I never asked the question. I'm curious, Mara, what are your experiences in similar situations? I think it's really hard for us to deal with competing experts.
turns.zh: "我从来没问出那个问题。"我很好奇，Moira，在类似的情形里你有什么经历？我觉得我们很难对付那些相互对立的专家。

turns.en: I can remember just done a podcast with Robin Powell in the UK who's very much into sort of the boring investments. I talked to him about some financial advice that we were being given as a family and all of the counterpoints that that advisor was giving for why the boring investments weren't good.
turns.zh: 我记得刚和英国的 Robin Powell 做过一期播客，他非常推崇那种无聊的投资。我跟他谈了我们家当时被给出的某些财务建议，以及那位顾问为了说明"无聊的投资为什么不好"所给出的一切反驳。

turns.en: And he just went, oh my, I understand why it's hard to stand in the presence of somebody who's telling you why this time it's different. Why this particular complexity of product is important for you and your family to have.
turns.zh: 他只是惊叹：天哪，我明白了——当有人告诉你"为什么这次不一样"、告诉你为什么这种产品的特殊复杂性对你的家庭很重要时，站在他面前有多难。

turns.en: And I will be behind you to make sure that we get out at just the right time if we need to get out. What do I know? What I know now is I have probably 7,000 more hours of statistics training than that guy ever had, but I didn't have a designation and I wasn't in that role.
turns.zh: "如果需要出局，我会支持你，确保我们恰好在正确的时机出去。"我懂什么呢？我现在懂的是：我大概比那家伙多受了七千个小时的统计学训练，可我没有头衔，也不在那个岗位上。

turns.en: And mostly we get just tired and we want somebody to take care of our stuff that we don't want to take care of. Somebody is saying that we could do better and that would make a difference in our life.
turns.zh: 而大多数时候，我们只是累了，想让某人来打理我们不想打理的那些东西。有人在说，我们本可以做得更好，那会改变我们的生活。

turns.en: Those are very compelling words. They don't necessarily activate greed. They activate a sense of responsibility that you should do this thing.
turns.zh: 那是很有说服力的话。它们未必激发贪婪，它们激发的是一种"你本该做这件事"的责任感。

turns.en: I think as just regular consumers, research, research, research, you can find out if your CFP has any regulatory strikes against him or her.
turns.zh: 我觉得，作为普通消费者，去做调查、调查、再调查，你可以查出你的 CFP 有没有对他或她的任何监管处罚记录。

turns.en: That's publicly available knowledge. You can find out who is this person behind the desk at the bank giving you advice and what allows them to be qualified.
turns.zh: 那是公开可得的信息。你可以查出柜台后面那个给你建议的人是谁，是什么让他们获得执业资格的。

turns.en: The challenge as we know now, Ben and Kermit, is that it's often hard for people who don't have huge amounts of money to get neutral, good, high quality advice.
turns.zh: 正如我们现在所知，Ben 和 Cameron，挑战在于：对那些没有一大笔钱的人来说，往往很难拿到中立、优质的建议。

turns.en: Because they gravitate towards product providers that are incentivized to sell them the products that they have, that they own. So that's an issue.
turns.zh: 因为他们会自然而然地偏向那些被激励去向客户推销自家产品的产品提供商，他们手里有什么就卖什么。这就是个问题。

turns.en: We asked one question earlier about what would be some warning signs. This isn't necessarily for the investor, the consumer. But one of the things that you need to know as a manager is that if your team, which was previously coherent and cohesive, and they all seem to be getting along, is suddenly there's weird stuff going on.
turns.zh: 我们前面问过一个关于警示信号的问题。这不一定是给投资人、给消费者看的。但作为管理者你需要知道的一点是：如果你的团队原本运转得很顺畅、很团结，大家看起来都相处得很好，突然之间冒出一些奇怪的事情。

turns.en: You're sensing alliances, you're sensing discontent. Somebody might be reporting bullying or intimidation. That is a really, really good sign that you have a fox in the hen house.
turns.zh: 你感觉到有人在拉帮结派，感觉到人心浮动。可能有人举报了霸凌或恐吓。这真的是一个非常好的信号——说明你的鸡舍里进了一只狐狸。

turns.en: That a psychopath has entered the mix or one of these snakes in suits. You need to investigate because they always cause difficulties in team functioning.
turns.zh: 也就是说，有一个心理变态者（psychopath）混了进来，或者混进了这么一条穿西装的毒蛇。你必须去调查，因为这类人一定会在团队运作中制造麻烦。

turns.en: So if that's going on as a manager, take note. That's a huge red flag. Each of you came into this project with such unique experiences and backgrounds, a tremendous amount of experience, relevant experience to this topic.
turns.zh: 所以如果你是管理者，发现这种情况正在发生，一定要留意。这是一个巨大的危险信号。你们两位带着各自独特的经历和背景参与这个项目，积累了极其丰富、也极其契合这个话题的经验。

turns.en: But what do you think your biggest learnings were from writing this book? I'm not sure I could answer that. I've written another hour. There is the importance of relationships within and without the firm.
turns.zh: 但你们觉得写这本书最大的收获是什么？我不确定我能回答这个问题。我又多聊了一个小时。其中一个收获，是认识到关系的重要性——无论是在公司内部还是公司外部。

turns.en: The importance of knowing myself and doing the work on myself. The importance of understanding we are all vulnerable. And one thing that we were really aware of as we went through the book was ensuring that people didn't read the book and say, well, that's okay because I would never do that.
turns.zh: 认识到了解自己的重要性，在自我上做功课的重要性。认识到我们每一个人都是脆弱的。我们在写书过程中始终非常留意的一点是，不要让读者读完之后说：那没事，因为这种事我永远不会做。

turns.en: And I did this through writing this with Moira is to understand where my own personal vulnerabilities are and that we are all incredibly delightfully and wonderfully human.
turns.zh: 而我和 Moira 一起写这本书的过程，恰恰让我看清了自己的个人脆弱之处在哪里，也让我明白我们是如此可爱、如此奇妙、如此鲜活的人。

turns.en: And that being kind to yourself is a super important part of your ethical health. One of the big learnings for me was about something called the illusion of superiority or the better than average effect, which is the notion that we often rank ourselves as being better drivers, better health nuts, whatever.
turns.zh: 善待自己，是你道德健康中极其重要的一部分。对我而言，一个大收获是关于一个叫"优越感错觉"（illusion of superiority）或"优于平均水平效应"（better than average effect）的东西，它的意思是，我们常常把自己评价成更好的司机、更懂养生的人，诸如此类。

turns.en: We see ourselves as being higher than average on a number of dimensions, which you can just sort of laugh at. But there's one domain where that illusion is on steroids.
turns.zh: 我们在很多维度上都把自己看得高于平均水平，这事儿你其实可以一笑置之。但有一个领域，这种错觉简直是被放大到了极致。

turns.en: And that is within the domain of morality. None of us want to contemplate the fact that we might just be normally ethical, average ethical. Well, of course, then better than that.
turns.zh: 那就是道德领域。我们谁都不愿意去设想，自己可能也就是个普普通通、平平常常守道德的人。当然了，我们都觉得自己比这还要更好一些。

turns.en: But the moral humility is something that the regulators, when we came back and we asked all of the people who we interviewed for the book, including you Cam, about how should one stay ethical?
turns.zh: 但道德上的谦逊（moral humility）——当我们回过头去采访书里涉及的所有人，包括你 Cam，问"一个人该怎么保持道德"的时候——

turns.en: Almost to a person, everybody said some version of there, but for the grace of God, go I. It could have been me and I'm just really lucky that life circumstances and the supports around me have helped keep me upright.
turns.zh: 几乎每个人给出的答案都是同一个意思的某个版本：若非托福佑，彼即是我（there but for the grace of God, go I）。那本可能是我，我只是很幸运，生活的境遇和我身边的支撑让我一直站得稳。

turns.en: Moral humility is something to be cultivated, to be welcomed. The second big learning for me is that we have to learn to tolerate being uncomfortable and to not treat it like it's a nuisance, but to treat that discomfort as meaningful data that we need to pause and name and explore.
turns.zh: 道德上的谦逊是一种需要培养、需要欢迎的东西。对我而言第二个大收获是：我们必须学会容忍那种不舒服的感觉，不要把它当成麻烦，而是把这种不适当作有意义的信号，需要我们停下来、说出它的名字、去探索它。

turns.en: And then the third learning for me was unequivocally, navigate your way to good employment. If you have any sense that something in your firm is wiffy, get out of there.
turns.zh: 对我而言第三个收获则是毫无疑问地：想办法走向一份好的工作。如果你对自家公司有任何一点感觉不对劲、有些可疑（wiffy），就赶紧离开。

turns.en: It will shape you in ways that you won't like and it will not protect you if the regulators come calling. So find good people to work for. Create your own firm someday if that's what it takes, but navigate your way.
turns.zh: 它会以你不喜欢的方式塑造你，而且一旦监管机构找上门，它不会保护你。所以要去找值得为之工作的好人。如果有必要，将来自己开一家公司，但一定要主动为自己规划好方向。

turns.en: Get the best qualifications that you possibly can for the position that you're interested in. Volunteer, network, find people, and keep yourself financially free.
turns.zh: 针对你感兴趣的岗位，去拿下你所能拿到的最好的资质。去做志愿者，去拓展人脉，去结识同行，同时让自己在财务上保持自由。

turns.en: Don't let yourself become overextended. Of course, everybody in society is dependent on their employer to pay their mortgage, but work your way up to having some degree of choice over these matters.
turns.zh: 别把自己拖入过度负债的境地。当然，社会上的每个人都依赖雇主来还自己的房贷，但要一步步往上走，直到你在这类事情上有一定程度的选择权。

turns.en: Our final question, how do you reach to find success in your lives? I know you're gonna ask this question because I've listened to your podcast.
turns.zh: 我们的最后一个问题：你们如何在各自的人生里找到成功？我知道你们一定会问这个问题，因为我听过你们的播客。

turns.en: It was a really interesting thought process as I went through this and I was walking along mulling it over because thinking walks are really good.
turns.zh: 在思考这个问题的过程中，我一路走一路琢磨，这真是一次很有意思的思维历程，因为边走边想（thinking walks）确实很有帮助。

turns.en: And the conclusion I came to was, I'm living it. I am, this is success. I have a job that fulfills me, that is congruent with my values. That feels amazing.
turns.zh: 我得出的结论是：我正身处其中。是的，这就是成功。我有一份让我感到充实、与我价值观相契合的工作。这种感觉太美好了。

turns.en: I can push things forward. We held a big event the other day about climate change. I can go out there and I can make that happen. That's amazing.
turns.zh: 我能把事情向前推进。前几天我们办了一场关于气候变化的大型活动，我可以站出来，让那件事真正发生。这太了不起了。

turns.en: I get to have written this amazing book with this amazing woman and asked this deep, deep question that we spent, I think two and a half years, almost three years contemplating and talking to people.
turns.zh: 我竟然有机会和这位了不起的女性一起写下这本了不起的书，提出了这个非常非常深刻的问题，我们花了——我想——两年半、差不多三年的时间来思考它、去访谈别人。

turns.en: I have amazing friends. I have amazing family. I have enough money. I don't lust after the Maserati's of this world. I get to go on holiday.
turns.zh: 我有很棒的朋友，有很棒家人，我有够花的钱。我不会对世界上那些玛莎拉蒂（Maserati）心痒难耐。我能去度假。

turns.en: I don't have to add up food as I go around the supermarket. I can give and I do time and money. I am basically living my version of success.
turns.zh: 我不必一边逛超市一边在心里算饭菜钱。我愿意付出，也确实付出了时间和金钱。基本上，我正在过着我这个版本的成功。

turns.en: And thank you for asking that question because it allowed me to say, I'm living it. I am successful. And that feels absolutely amazing. You know, it depends on the day.
turns.zh: 谢谢你们问这个问题，因为它让我得以说出：我正身处其中，我是成功的。这种感觉真的太美好了。你知道，这也得看具体是哪一天。

turns.en: Some days, success feels like, I remembered that password finally, but on a more global perspective, that Philippa was taking. It has so much to do with having some measure of control I'm aware of or freedom to choose.
turns.zh: 有些日子，成功的感觉就是——我终于想起那个密码了。但如果从 Philippa 所说的那种更宏观的视角来看，它有太多关乎你能否拥有一定的掌控感，或者说选择的自由。

turns.en: And I'm aware of just how much privilege I have in being able to choose some of the things and that in turn, choosing the right things opens you up to having more freedom to make good choices.
turns.zh: 我很清楚自己能选择某些事情，这份特权有多重；而这种选择，选对了事情，反过来又会让你拥有更多自由，去做出好的选择。

turns.en: But for me, it comes down to things like relationships, overachievement, wholeness over accumulation. I really want to be a safe harbor and a force for good in this world.
turns.zh: 但对我来说，归结到最后是这些东西：关系，"完整"（wholeness）胜过"累积"。我真的很想成为这个世间的一个安全港湾、一股向善的力量。

turns.en: I want to not disappoint the people that matter to me, my family, my children, my friends. Not that momentary disappointment of, no, you can't have a cookie, but I want to be somebody that they are proud to have known or to be related to.
turns.zh: 我不想让对我重要的人失望——我的家人、我的孩子、我的朋友。不是那种"不行，你不能吃饼干"的当下失望，而是我想成为一个让他们为认识我、为与我有血缘关系而感到骄傲的人。

turns.en: That alignment between values and action under pressure and the things that could be true of you no matter where you fall on the socioeconomic spectrum, those markers of integrity are what really stand out to me now.
turns.zh: 那种在压力之下、价值观与行动之间的一致性，那种无论你落在社会经济光谱的哪一端都可能具备的品质——这些正直（integrity）的标志，如今才是真正让我看重的东西。

turns.en: Can I ask you to a question if that's all right? Sure. What stood out from the book to you two when you read it? The biggest thing for me was just the concept of behavioral ethics, which I think is a big part of what the book ends up being about, I think.
turns.zh: 我可以问你们一个问题吗，如果方便的话？当然。你们自己读这本书的时候，书里什么最让你们印象深刻？对我而言最大的收获，是 behavioral ethics、即"行为伦理学"这个概念，我觉得这正是这本书最终的落脚点。

turns.en: This idea that we can have a rational ethical framework and people can know what they should do and they can know right from wrong. But for various reasons, they can still end up doing bad things.
turns.zh: 这个想法是：我们可以有一套理性的道德框架，人们可以知道自己该做什么，可以明辨是非。但出于种种原因，他们最终仍然可能做出坏事。

turns.en: As we talked about earlier, you need to have culture. You need to have systems in place. You need to check in with yourself and be very in tune with yourself to understand where your vulnerabilities are.
turns.zh: 正如我们前面谈到的，你需要有文化，你需要有一套运转的系统。你需要时常自省，非常敏锐地觉察自己，去理解自己的脆弱之处在哪里。

turns.en: But just that concept of, just like with other parts of life, we can have rational frameworks for things and we can say what people should do in certain situations.
turns.zh: 就是这个概念——就像生活的其他方面一样，我们可以为很多事情搭建理性的框架，可以说出人们在各具体情境下该怎么做。

turns.en: But that's often going to be very different from what they will actually do and understanding where those vulnerabilities are is really, I would argue more important to acting ethically than understanding right from wrong.
turns.zh: 但那往往与他们实际会做的事情截然不同，而理解这些脆弱之处在哪里，我认为比单纯明辨是非，对"有道德地行动"来说重要得多。

turns.en: I actually sent myself a picture, took a screenshot of the moral operating system. I could tell you put a lot of work into that. At least I believe you did.
turns.zh: 我其实给自己拍了一张道德操作系统（moral operating system）的照片，截了个图。我能看出你们在这上面下了很大功夫。至少我相信你们下了功夫。

turns.en: And just to go through that wheel, now you have to spend a little bit of time with it, but it's such a thought provoking each one of the pieces of pies on that wheel is pretty clear and can really cause someone to think and it's worthwhile time to be spent.
turns.zh: 就那样把那个轮盘走一遍——你确实需要花点时间和它相处——但它太发人深省了，那个轮盘上每一块饼图都相当清晰，真的能引发人去思考，这段时间花得值得。

turns.en: So I thought that was really nice to kind of encapsulate everything that was in the book, especially being in the industry. It's an interesting read and it's an easy read.
turns.zh: 所以我觉得，它把书里的所有内容很巧妙地浓缩在了一起，尤其是身在这个行业里的人。这是一本很有意思、也很好读的书。

turns.en: So kudos to both of you on this great accomplishment. This was an enormous amount of work clearly. Thank you for noting the behavioral ethics part of it, Ben.
turns.zh: 所以，向你们两位致以祝贺，这是了不起的成就。这显然是巨大的工作量。

turns.en: I think that that's been the part that's been missing for me within all of the financial ethics training is where are people in this? Obviously I have a bias to that as a psychologist, but the regulators begged us to help people understand that it's their humanity that needs to come into play and that includes their own biases and things that you can't just will yourself out of.
turns.zh: 谢谢你点出了其中的行为伦理学部分，Ben。我觉得，在我见过的所有金融道德培训里，恰恰缺了这一环——处在这个情境里的人，他们自己在哪里？作为一名心理学家，我在这件事上当然有偏向——但监管机构请求我们帮助人们理解：需要被纳入考量的，是他们的人性，而人性里包括他们自己的偏见，包括那些你无法单凭意志力就摆脱的东西。

turns.en: You need to learn how to work with them. I love the fact that you're gonna go and do the moral operating system work. We wanted to give people something actionable to take away because that behavioral ethics piece does need that.
turns.zh: 你需要学会如何与之共处。我很喜欢你打算去做那套道德操作系统练习这件事。我们想给人们一些可以真正带回去、可以动手做的东西，因为行为伦理学这一块确实需要这个。

turns.en: And your advice to read this as a study group, I think that's wise counsel. Yeah, and we would love to hear from people as and when they do.
turns.zh: 而你们建议以读书会的方式来读这本书，我认为这是非常明智的忠告。是的，我们也乐意在人们读完之后随时听听他们的反馈。

turns.en: I mean, we've sent this book out into the world. Our greatest hope is that it actually makes a difference. And I think we said the other day we will have failed if it's made no difference to the world, that's what we want.
turns.zh: 我的意思是，我们已经把这本书送进了这个世界。我们最大的心愿，是它真的能带来一点改变。我想前几天我们说过：如果它对这个世界毫无影响，那我们就失败了——这正是我们所希望的。

turns.en: So we would really genuinely love to hear from people as they run through the book and please do ask his questions. Terrific, well, Philip, it's great to meet you.
turns.zh: 所以我们真的很、很真诚地想听听大家把这本书读下来的心得，也请一定来提问。太棒了。好，Philippa，很高兴认识你。

turns.en: Moira, your long-term friends are great to see you again. As always, congrats on the book. Thank you so much. Thank you. Thanks, guys. All right, Ben, incredible conversation, pretty incredible book.
turns.zh: Moira，你这些老朋友，很高兴再见到你们。一如既往，恭喜你们出了这本书。非常感谢。谢谢你。谢谢你们，各位。好了 Ben，这是一场精彩的对话，一本相当精彩的书。

turns.en: I think this is going to be widely read and picked up by the industry around the world. I mean, we jokingly were talking before we started recording, I asked them if they were on the proverbial circuit because each fall, at least from my take at the industry, the fall season really ramps up with events.
turns.zh: 我觉得这本书会被广泛阅读，会被世界各地的整个行业拿去研读。我的意思是，我们正式开始录音前还开玩笑聊过，我问她们是不是在跑那个俗称的"巡回宣传"（the circuit），因为至少从我对行业的观察来看，每到秋天，行业活动的节奏就会明显加快。

turns.en: And I think that they should be, and I hope they will be on many stages around the industry for quite a while. As we were talking about that with them, I was thinking that we should be having our teams read this book, or at the very least, going through the thing that you talked about at the end of the conversation there, Cameron, about creating your own moral operating system, which they give step-by-step instructions for in the book.
turns.zh: 我觉得她们应该去，也希望她们接下来很长一段时间里，能站上行业里许许多多的舞台。在和她们聊这些的时候，我在想，我们真该让整个团队来读这本书，或者至少，去走一遍 Cam 你在对话结尾提到的那件事——创建你自己的道德操作系统，书里给了一步步的操作指引。

turns.en: It's pretty cool. I've read it. I have not sat down and gone through the exercise yet, but it's 12 steps, I believe. It is 12. Guides you through thinking through your own moral operating system, which sets you up, as we talked about in the podcast, to deal with behavioral ethics, to set yourself up to be prepared to deal with the situations where ethics can lapse.
turns.zh: 这挺酷的。我读过了。我还没有正儿八经坐下来把这个练习做完，但据我理解它有 12 个步骤。确实是 12 个。它会引导你梳理出自己的道德操作系统，正如我们在播客里谈到的，这让你为应对行为伦理所带来的问题做好准备，让你提前准备好去应对那些道德可能失守的情境。

turns.en: To set you up, but also your organization, both structurally, but also culturally. Systems and culture are huge for this. And you have new people.
turns.zh: 它不仅为你做准备，也为你的组织做准备——既在结构层面，也在文化层面。对于这件事，系统和文化都至关重要。而且你会遇到新人。

turns.en: They talk about what kind of new people and the older people. New people, they just don't know what they don't know. So it can be unintentional, bad behavior, but older people, depending on the incentive systems, perhaps, can cause just the culture.
turns.zh: 他们谈到是怎样的新人，以及老人。新人，他们只是不知道自己不知道什么。所以不良行为可能是无心的；但老人呢，取决于激励机制，也许就是文化本身出了问题。

turns.en: Culture and systems. Where you are, who you're surrounded by. I didn't say this when we were talking tomorrow in Philippa, but I was thinking it.
turns.zh: 文化和系统。你所处的位置，你身边围绕着什么样的人。Philippa，我们聊的时候我没说出口，但我心里在想。

turns.en: One of the things that I'm most proud of with what we've created at PWL is that we are the firm where people who want to be sure that they're doing the right thing, they gravitate to us.
turns.zh: 我们在 PWL 打造的事业里，我最引以为豪的事情之一就是：我们是这样一家公司——那些真心想确保自己做对事情的人，会自然地向我们聚拢。

turns.en: Whether they're employees coming to work here or peers in the industry who look at what PWL is doing, I at least believe that we have put ourselves in that position.
turns.zh: 无论是来这儿工作的员工，还是同行里关注 PWL 在做什么的人，我至少相信，我们已经把自己放在了那个位置上。

turns.en: Well, I remember the conversation we talked about when one of our advisors joined saying, I just hope it's like how you sound on the podcast.
turns.zh: 我记得有这么一次对话，我们的某位理财师刚加入时说过：我只希望这儿真像你们在播客里听起来的那样。

turns.en: Well, we hear that from clients too, for sure. As far as we know, and we have gotten this specific feedback, we are at least as good or whatever you want to call it as we present ourselves to be on the podcast.
turns.zh: 嗯，我们从客户那里也听到过同样的话，肯定听到过。至少据我们所知，从我们收到的这类具体反馈来看，我们至少和我们在这个播客里呈现出来的样子一样好——随你怎么称呼它。

turns.en: Anyways, if you're in the industry, I would argue this is a must read book. I think it's a good read for kind of anyone who's in the working world.
turns.zh: 总之，如果你在行业里，我会说这是一本必读的书。我觉得它对任何身处职场的人都是一本好书。

turns.en: And if you're interested in the subject, of course, but certainly if you're in this industry. We also had a good conversation about product providers.
turns.zh: 如果你对这一主题感兴趣，那当然必读；但如果你恰恰身在这个行业，那就更是如此。我们还聊到了一段关于产品提供商（product providers）的精彩对话。

turns.en: This goes back to a few episodes we've had and you're talking about ETF slop, for example. Why do advisors choose certain products and how does the industry get pitched certain products?
turns.zh: 这会让我们回想前几期聊过的内容，比如你谈到 ETF slop（ETF 里掺的水）——为什么理财师会选择某些产品，行业又是怎么被推销某些产品的？

turns.en: Yeah, there's a whole section of the book. We've got, okay, financial professionals, financial advisors that they can enter into misconduct that harms investors.
turns.zh: 是的，书里有一整个章节。我们讲到，好，金融从业者、理财师，他们可能会实施损害投资人的不当行为（misconduct）。

turns.en: But you can also have financial product providers who can enter into misconduct or borderline misconduct when they're selling financial products to financial advisors who will then go and sell the product to their clients.
turns.zh: 但也可能有金融产品提供商，在把金融产品卖给那些会再把产品转售给自己客户的理财师时，实施不当行为、或者说擦边不当行为。

turns.en: And a lot of that comes back to complexity, selling the idea of exclusivity, all that kind of stuff. Do you want to give us some more background on Moira?
turns.zh: 而这里面很多问题都归结于复杂性，归结于把"专属性"这个概念卖给客户，那一类的东西。你要不要给我们再多介绍一下 Moira 的背景？

turns.en: So Moira, as I mentioned in the introduction, she's a clinical neuropsychologist, family wealth consultant and executive coach. She's Canadian based in Winnipeg.
turns.zh: 好，Moira，就像我在开头介绍的，她是一名临床神经心理学家（clinical neuropsychologist）、家族财富顾问和高管教练。她是加拿大人，常驻在温尼伯（Winnipeg）。

turns.en: She is an incredible resource for wealthy families and people. She works a lot with advisors, but she also works directly with clients. When we at PWL realize that we are out of our depth from the perspective of psychological issues related to money with a client, we will bring Moira in as a third party and she will engage with clients directly to help them work through those issues.
turns.zh: 对于富裕家族和个人来说，她是一个了不起的资源。她和很多理财师合作，但也直接服务客户。当我们在 PWL 意识到，遇到与客户金钱相关的心理层面的问题时，已经超出了我们的能力边界，我们就会把 Moira 作为第三方请进来，她会直接与客户接触，帮他们把这些心结理清楚。

turns.en: So she's been a fantastic partner for us in that sense. A very interesting and unique skill set that she has, that she brings to writing this book, also just her as a professional.
turns.zh: 所以在这个意义上，她是我们的一个非常好的伙伴。她自身那种非常有趣、非常独特的专业能力，不仅为写这本书带来了价值，作为一个专业人士本身也是如此。

turns.en: She's a fascinating person. And Philippa, who we just met for the first time today, we've known Moira for a long time, but Philippa, we just met, she's a practicing lawyer with 20 years, specializing in financial services litigation and dual qualified as a solicitor and a financial advisor.
turns.zh: 她是一个非常迷人的人。还有 Philippa，我们今天才第一次见面——我们认识 Moira 很久了，但 Philippa 是刚认识。她是一名执业律师，有 20 年经验，专攻金融服务诉讼（financial services litigation），并且同时具备事务律师（solicitor）和理财师的双重资格。

turns.en: And she's now recently become the CEO of Paradigm Norton, which is a UK financial planning firm. So she's basically gone from suing financial advisors to leading a financial advisory firm.
turns.zh: 她最近刚刚成为 Paradigm Norton 的首席执行官，那是一家英国的理财规划公司。所以她基本上是从"起诉理财师"，变成了"领导一家理财咨询公司"。

turns.en: We talked about the large case she did on behalf of British Steel. She regularly speaks in industry events and well-known certainly in the UK financial planning industry.
turns.zh: 我们聊到了她代表英国钢铁公司（British Steel）做的那个大案子。她经常在行业活动上发言，在英国理财规划行业里也确实是知名人物。

turns.en: And they tell at the front end of the conversation, as we know now how they actually met to decide on writing this book, which I thought was super interesting too, just kind of two minds meeting at a conference and there you go, there's the work that comes out of it.
turns.zh: 她们在对话开头也讲到——我们现在知道了——她们究竟是怎么认识的、又是怎么决定一起写这本书的，我也觉得那特别有意思：就是两个头脑在一次会议上相遇，于是就有了，就有了由此诞生的这部作品。

turns.en: They realized they complimented each other in a way that they were gonna be able to create some information that was unique, which I think they've been successful in doing.
turns.zh: 她们意识到彼此刚好形成互补，这意味着她们能够创造出某种独特的东西，而我觉得她们也确实成功地做到了这一点。

turns.en: Awesome, anything else to add Ben? No, I'm kind of tempted to go through the moral operating system steps, but it's probably too much to do in the audio format.
turns.zh: 太棒了，Ben，还有什么要补充的吗？没有，我其实有点想把道德操作系统那几个步骤走一遍，但在音频里做这个恐怕太多了。

turns.en: I suggest people pick up a copy of the book and go through it themselves. It's a really interesting exercise. Agreed, okay, great conversation.
turns.zh: 我建议人们去买一本这个书，自己动手走一遍。这真的是一次很有意思的练习。同意。好，一场很棒的对话。
